misconceptions.misconception: Polystyrene has a constant relative molecular mass like a small molecule
misconceptions.why: Students think polymers have fixed size like typical organic molecules
misconceptions.correction: Addition polymerisation involves random chain termination. Chains stop growing at different times, so each polymer molecule has a different chain length and different Mᵣ
misconceptions.examTip: Mark scheme always mentions 'range of' or 'variable' molecular mass for polymers

misconceptions.misconception: Increasing temperature increases collision frequency, so reaction is faster
misconceptions.why: Students only think about the kinetic theory part, not activation energy
misconceptions.correction: Temperature mainly increases the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Eₐ (activation energy). Collision frequency increase is small. More molecules reach Eₐ = much faster reaction
misconceptions.examTip: Always mention 'greater proportion with E ≥ Eₐ' or 'more effective collisions'

misconceptions.why: Confusion between battery polarity and electrolysis cell polarity
misconceptions.correction: In electrolysis: anode = positive (attracts anions), cathode = negative (attracts cations). This is opposite to a battery cell
misconceptions.examTip: Watch the diagram carefully—follow the power supply connections, not memory
